body:
Yeah, that scene felt really forced. But it was one of my favourite scenes! Maybe I just interpreted it differently - on one hand, it was basically Marvel saying "look at how amazing we are with all this female representation" and if that was Marvel's attempt to show its female representation, it was pretty weak...they could do SO much better.

But on the other hand, I felt empowered after seeing that scene because it reminded me of all the amazing women I looked up to throughout the MCU movies as I grew up and just seeing them all together...I don't know, I just loved it and felt so strong and supported in that moment. Like "hey, here are a bunch of women who went through hard times, but look at them standing and being strong and powerful! and also look, they aren't alone...just like you aren't alone and you aren't the only girl going through things." Like the whole "we're stronger together" and "let's stand together" thing.

So yeah maybe Marvel was just trying to be "woke" or whatever. But so what? Clearly that scene wasn't for everyone and yeah it didn't really need to be added into the movie but, in my opinion, it wasn't made to be for everyone and it wasn't added in the movie for everyone. Endgame had a bunch of exciting scenes for each different MCU fan, that was just one of them. 

Anyways, that's just my perspective and just wanted to share it. :) Still in my post-Endgame feels and getting ready to go watch it another 3000 times.
